statement: The function returns a result r. Let k be the integer value of r. Call a contiguous subarray nums[a..b), where 0 <= a < b <= len(nums), strictly increasing if nums[i] < nums[i+1] for every i with a <= i < b-1, and strictly decreasing if nums[i] > nums[i+1] for every i with a <= i < b-1. Then k is the greatest integer with 1 <= k <= len(nums) for which there exists a with 0 <= a and a+k <= len(nums) such that nums[a..a+k) is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing. Equivalently, k is the maximum length of a nonempty contiguous subarray of nums that is either strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 50, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 50.
